item.title: We had to work very hard for the win – Ikanivere
item.description: Navitalai Naivalurua · 22/11/2026 After the FIJI Water Flying Fijians claimed their first win in the Nations Championship competition this morning, captain Tevita Ikanivere admitted that they had to work very hard for the victory.
item.content:encoded:
Navitalai Naivalurua · 22/11/2026

After the FIJI Water Flying Fijians claimed their first win in the Nations Championship competition this morning, captain Tevita Ikanivere admitted that they had to work very hard for the victory.

Fiji ran in three tries to claim a 21-16 victory over Italy.

Ikanivere says they knew the Italians would not give up easily, and he is looking forward to facing them again next week.

He adds that he is proud of the efforts of the players.

Meanwhile, the Flying Fijians will face Italy again at 4.40am next Saturday.

item.title: All Blacks and Springboks suffer second Nations Championship defeats
item.description: Navitalai Naivalurua · 22/11/2026 The All Blacks and South Africa suffered their second defeats in the Nations Championship this morning, leaving South Africa in first place and New Zealand second in the Southern Hemisphere standings.
item.content:encoded:
Navitalai Naivalurua · 22/11/2026

The All Blacks and South Africa suffered their second defeats in the Nations Championship this morning, leaving South Africa in first place and New Zealand second in the Southern Hemisphere standings.

The All Blacks lost to England 37-12, while the Springboks were edged out by Ireland 20-17.

Last week, four of the five Southern Hemisphere teams lost their matches, with Argentina the only exception.

Argentina are currently third on the points table and will take on France at 8.10 this morning.

Also at 8.10 this morning, the Wallabies will face Wales.

item.title: Arsenal extend Premier League lead after 2-all draw with Newcastle
item.description: Arsenal have moved six points clear at the top of the English Premier League following a 2-all draw against Newcastle United this morning. Arsenal took the lead through Eberechi Eze, who finished with a first-time shot.
item.content:encoded:
Arsenal have moved six points clear at the top of the English Premier League following a 2-all draw against Newcastle United this morning.

Arsenal took the lead through Eberechi Eze, who finished with a first-time shot.

However, a mistake by Martin Odegaard allowed Harvey Barnes to equalise for Newcastle before Malick Thiaw put the home side ahead.

Arsenal responded through Noni Madueke, who scored with the team's first shot of the second half to secure a point.

Arsenal goalkeeper David Raya was also forced off the field with a shoulder injury.

In other matches, Manchester City and Fulham played out a 1-1 draw, Bournemouth defeated Nottingham Forest 2-0, Leeds United thrashed Chelsea 4-1 while Aston Villa and Sunderland played out a nil-all draw.

Arsenal is leading 28 points followed by Brighton with 22 points, Manchester City is third with 22 points while Bournemouth is fourth with 18 points.
